plain.text: The apostles and believers in Judea heard that Gentiles had received God's word. In Jerusalem, some criticised Peter: "You went into the house of uncircumcised men and ate with them." Peter explained everything step by step: his vision, the men from Caesarea, and how the Holy Spirit came on the Gentiles as he began to speak, just as on the believers at the beginning. "If God gave them the same gift he gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to think I could stand in God's way?" They had no further objections and praised God: "So then, even to Gentiles God has granted repentance that leads to life."

Believers scattered by the persecution after Stephen's death travelled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch, telling the message only to Jews. But some began to speak to Greeks in Antioch too, telling them the good news about the Lord Jesus. The Lord's hand was with them, and many believed. The church in Jerusalem sent Barnabas to Antioch. He was glad to see what God's grace had done and encouraged them all to stay true to the Lord. He was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul and brought him to Antioch, where they taught great numbers for a year. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch. When a prophet named Agabus predicted a severe famine, the disciples decided to send help to the believers in Judea, each according to their ability, through Barnabas and Saul.

summary.bigIdea: The Jerusalem church accepts that God welcomes Gentiles, and in Antioch a new church grows and becomes known as "Christians".
points: Peter explains how God gave the Spirit to Gentiles, and the church praises God.
The good news spreads to Greeks in Antioch, and Barnabas encourages them.
The disciples are first called Christians, and they send help to Judea in a famine.
summary.reflection: Barnabas "was glad" when he saw God's grace at work. Where can you see God's grace at work around you?
